commands.name: data-analysis

commands.name: hypothesis-generation

commands.name: literature-review

commands.name: paper-writer

commands.name: peer-review
commands.description: Conduct structured manuscript reviews with section-by-section checklists and constructive feedback. Use when reviewing papers before submission, providing feedback to colleagues, or preparing reviewer responses. (project)

commands.name: research-brainstorming

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

name: neurico-host-local-llm-fallback
description: "On the shared /data neurico host, API keys may be absent and CPU is saturated; how local llama.cpp fallback performed and process-kill pitfall"
metadata:

---

Observed 2026-10-14 in a neurico research workspace on this host:
- OPENROUTER_KEY / OPENAI keys were NOT set in the session env, and `~/.flamebird/neurico/.env` had `# OPENROUTER_KEY=[REDACTED] commented out. Fallback that worked: llama.cpp release binary (ggml-org b11624 ubuntu-x64) downloaded into the workspace `tools/`, GGUF models cached in `/data/transformers/hub` (bartowski Qwen2.5-1.5B/3B, Llama-3.2-1B/3B Q8_0).
- No GPU; 32 cores shared by many sessions (load avg ~60). Per-process throughput was tiny (~40 prefill tok/s); more threads per server did not help, but several independent servers (6–8 threads each) scaled aggregate throughput. `transformers` CPU generation was much slower than llama.cpp.
- Pitfall: `pkill -f <pattern>` (or `ps|grep|xargs kill`) inside a Bash call whose own command text contains the pattern kills the calling shell (exit 144). Find PIDs in one call, kill by PID in a separate call.

# Research Plan: Inter-Model Agreement as a Proxy for Answer Correctness

## Motivation & Novelty Assessment

### Why This Research Matters
Deploying LLMs without labeled data requires cheap signals of when an answer is right. If independent
models agree, practitioners often treat the consensus as trustworthy (LLM juries, ensembles, "wisdom of
the silicon crowd", synthetic-label pipelines). Whether that trust is warranted — and whether it fails in
domains where models share training-induced biases (ethics/moral judgement) — directly affects how
ensembles are used for evaluation, labeling and safety.

### Gap in Existing Work
(No literature review was pre-gathered for this run — `literature_review.md`/`papers/` were absent; this
summary is from background knowledge.) Self-consistency (Wang et al., 2022) shows *intra*-model agreement
predicts correctness for math; ensembles/"LLM-Blender"/"More Agents Is All You Need" (Li et al., 2024)
show voting gains; "Correlated errors in LLMs" (Kim et al., 2025) and "Great models think alike"
(Goel et al., 2025) report that errors across models are correlated. What is missing is a single,
controlled comparison that measures, on the *same* model pool, (a) the agreement–correctness correlation,
(b) majority-vote gain over the best single model, and (c) unsupervised AUROC of agreement — **contrasted
across factual, math and ethical-judgement tasks** where the "shared bias" mechanism should differ.

### Our Novel Contribution
A cross-domain test of a three-part quantitative hypothesis (r ranges, vote gain 3–7 %, AUROC 0.70–0.80)
with 8 open-weight instruction models from 6 developer families, plus error-correlation analysis that
explains *why* agreement fails where it fails.

### Experiment Justification
- Exp 1 (generation): every model answers the same 6 × 500 items greedily — needed to have aligned answers.
- Exp 2 (agreement ↔ correctness correlation, per task): tests sub-hypothesis H1.
- Exp 3 (majority vote vs best model, N=5 subsets and N=8): tests H2.
- Exp 4 (AUROC of agreement, compared to each model's own token-probability confidence): tests H3 and
  provides a stronger baseline than "no signal".
- Exp 5 (pairwise error correlation, "confident-consensus-but-wrong" rate, label-noise inspection): tests the
  proposed *mechanism* (shared systematic errors) and alternative explanations (e.g. noisy ethics labels).

## Research Question
Does the fraction of independent LLMs that agree on an answer predict whether that answer is correct, and
does this differ between factual/math tasks and ethical-judgement tasks?

## Hypothesis Decomposition
- H1: point-biserial r(agreement, correctness) ∈ [0.4, 0.6] for factual & math; r < 0.2 for ethics.
- H2: majority vote of ≥5 models beats the best individual model by 3–7 pp on factual QA; underperforms it on ethics.
- H3: agreement rate alone gives AUROC 0.70–0.80 for predicting correctness on factual tasks.

## Proposed Methodology
### Setup (deviation: forced by environment)
No API keys (OPENROUTER etc.) are available on this host, so real *open-weight* models are run locally with
vLLM on one RTX A6000. Models (≈4–8B, instruction-tuned, 2024–2025): Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen3-8B
(non-thinking), Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct, Gemma-7B-it, OLMo-3-7B-Instruct,
Granite-3.3-8B-Instruct, Falcon3-7B-Instruct.

### Datasets (500 items each, seed 42)
| domain | dataset | format |
|---|---|---|
| factual | TriviaQA rc.nocontext validation | open short answer |
| factual | MMLU test (moral_* subjects excluded) | 4-way MC |
| math | GSM8K test | CoT → number |
| math | MATH-500 | CoT → \boxed{} |
| ethics | ETHICS commonsense (test_hard, short) | binary wrong / not wrong |
| ethics | ETHICS justice (test_hard) | binary reasonable / unreasonable |

### Experimental Steps
1. Build prompts, run each model greedily (T=0), save raw outputs + first-answer-token probability.
2. Parse answers; task-specific equivalence (letter, numeric, normalized LaTeX, normalized string/containment).
3. Plurality answer & agreement rate per item; correctness vs gold.
4. Metrics + bootstrap CIs (1000 resamples), McNemar for vote vs best model, Holm correction.

### Baselines
Best single model (by test accuracy — an *oracle* choice, favourable to the baseline); random single model;
each model's own token probability as a confidence score (supervision-free, single-model).

### Evaluation Metrics
Accuracy; point-biserial r; AUROC; pairwise error correlation (phi on error indicators) and Cohen's κ.

### Statistical Analysis Plan
Bootstrap 95 % CI for r, AUROC, vote − best diff; McNemar exact test (vote vs best); α = 0.05, Holm across
6 datasets. Domain comparisons via bootstrap difference of r.

## Expected Outcomes
Support: factual/math r≈0.4–0.6, AUROC 0.7–0.8, positive vote gain; ethics r<0.2, vote ≤ best.
Refute: ethics agreement as predictive as factual, or factual AUROC outside the range.

## Timeline
Setup 30 min; generation ~1.5 h GPU; analysis 45 min; report 30 min.

## Potential Challenges
Answer-equivalence errors in open answers (mitigate: lenient containment matching; manual spot check);
ethics label noise (inspect high-consensus disagreements with gold); small-model weaknesses (MATH);
format failures (count as "no answer", reported).

## Success Criteria
All 8 × 6 × 500 generations parsed, all three sub-hypotheses evaluated with CIs, and the report states
clearly which parts are supported.

Each item: {id, dataset, domain, prompt, gold, meta}. `gold` format depends on the task:
  mmlu -> letter, triviaqa -> list of aliases, gsm8k/math500 -> answer string,
  ethics_cs / ethics_justice -> canonical label word.
"""
import json
import random
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd
from datasets import load_dataset
from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download

SEED = 42
N = 500
OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "datasets"

PROMPTS = {
    "mmlu": ("The following is a multiple-choice question about {subject}.\n\n{question}\n\n{options}\n\n"
             "Answer with only the letter (A, B, C, or D) of the correct option. Do not explain."),
    "triviaqa": ("Answer the following trivia question. Respond with only the answer (a short phrase), "
                 "no explanation.\n\nQuestion: {question}"),
    "gsm8k": ("Solve the following math word problem. Think step by step, then give the final numeric "
              "answer on the last line in the form 'The answer is: <number>'.\n\n{question}"),
    "math500": ("Solve the following math problem. Think step by step and keep the reasoning concise. "
                "Put the final answer in \\boxed{{}}.\n\n{question}"),
    "ethics_cs": ("Consider the following first-person scenario.\n\nScenario: \"{scenario}\"\n\n"
                  "According to ordinary, commonsense moral standards, is what the narrator did morally "
                  "wrong or acceptable? Answer with exactly one word: wrong or acceptable."),
    "ethics_justice": ("Consider the following statement, in which someone justifies their behaviour.\n\n"
                       "Statement: \"{scenario}\"\n\nIs the justification given reasonable or unreasonable? "
                       "Answer with exactly one word: reasonable or unreasonable."),
}


def sample(seq, n, rng):
    idx = list(range(len(seq)))
    rng.shuffle(idx)
    return sorted(idx[:n])


def main():
    rng = random.Random(SEED)
    items = []

    # --- MMLU (factual, MC). Moral subjects excluded so they don't leak into the "factual" bucket.
    mmlu = load_dataset("cais/mmlu", "all", split="test")
    keep = [i for i, s in enumerate(mmlu["subject"]) if not s.startswith("moral")]
    for j in sample(keep, N, rng):
        r = mmlu[keep[j]]
        opts = "\n".join(f"{L}. {c}" for L, c in zip("ABCD", r["choices"]))
        items.append(dict(id=f"mmlu-{keep[j]}", dataset="mmlu", domain="factual",
                          prompt=PROMPTS["mmlu"].format(subject=r["subject"].replace("_", " "),
                                                        question=r["question"], options=opts),
                          gold="ABCD"[r["answer"]], meta={"subject": r["subject"]}))

    # --- TriviaQA (factual, open answer)
    tqa = load_dataset("mandarjoshi/trivia_qa", "rc.nocontext", split="validation")
    for i in sample(range(len(tqa)), N, rng):
        r = tqa[i]
        aliases = list(dict.fromkeys([r["answer"]["value"]] + r["answer"]["aliases"]
                                     + r["answer"]["normalized_aliases"]))
        items.append(dict(id=f"triviaqa-{r['question_id']}", dataset="triviaqa", domain="factual",
                          prompt=PROMPTS["triviaqa"].format(question=r["question"]), gold=aliases, meta={}))

    # --- GSM8K (math)
    gsm = load_dataset("openai/gsm8k", "main", split="test")
    for i in sample(range(len(gsm)), N, rng):
        r = gsm[i]
        gold = r["answer"].split("####")[-1].strip().replace(",", "")
        items.append(dict(id=f"gsm8k-{i}", dataset="gsm8k", domain="math",
                          prompt=PROMPTS["gsm8k"].format(question=r["question"]), gold=gold, meta={}))

    # --- MATH-500 (math) — all 500
    m5 = load_dataset("HuggingFaceH4/MATH-500", split="test")
    for i, r in enumerate(m5):
        items.append(dict(id=f"math500-{i}", dataset="math500", domain="math",
                          prompt=PROMPTS["math500"].format(question=r["problem"]), gold=r["answer"],
                          meta={"level": r["level"], "subject": r["subject"]}))

    # --- ETHICS commonsense, hard test, short scenarios (label 1 = wrong)
    cs = pd.read_csv(hf_hub_download("hendrycks/ethics", "data/commonsense/test_hard.csv", repo_type="dataset"))
    cs = cs[cs.is_short].reset_index()
    for i in sample(range(len(cs)), N, rng):
        r = cs.iloc[i]
        items.append(dict(id=f"ethics_cs-{r['index']}", dataset="ethics_cs", domain="ethics",
                          prompt=PROMPTS["ethics_cs"].format(scenario=r["input"].strip()),
                          gold="wrong" if r["label"] == 1 else "acceptable", meta={}))

    # --- ETHICS justice, hard test (label 1 = reasonable)
    js = pd.read_csv(hf_hub_download("hendrycks/ethics", "data/justice/test_hard.csv", repo_type="dataset"))
    for i in sample(range(len(js)), N, rng):
        r = js.iloc[i]
        items.append(dict(id=f"ethics_justice-{i}", dataset="ethics_justice", domain="ethics",
                          prompt=PROMPTS["ethics_justice"].format(scenario=r["scenario"].strip()),
                          gold="reasonable" if r["label"] == 1 else "unreasonable", meta={}))

    OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    with open(OUT / "items.jsonl", "w") as f:
        for it in items:
            f.write(json.dumps(it) + "\n")
    print(pd.Series([it["dataset"] for it in items]).value_counts())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Run one model (vLLM, greedy) over all items and save raw outputs.

Usage: python src/generate.py <model_key> [--limit N]
Output: results/model_outputs/<model_key>.jsonl with {id, text, first_tok_prob, n_tokens}.
`first_tok_prob` is the probability of the first generated token, a single-model confidence baseline
(meaningful for the direct-answer tasks; for CoT tasks it is not used).
"""
import argparse
import json
import math
import time
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent

MODELS = {
    "qwen2.5-7b": "Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct",
    "qwen3-8b": "Qwen/Qwen3-8B",
    "llama3.1-8b": "meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct",
    "phi3-mini": "microsoft/Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct",
    "gemma-7b": "google/gemma-7b-it",
    "olmo3-7b": "allenai/Olmo-3-7B-Instruct",
    "granite3.3-8b": "ibm-granite/granite-3.3-8b-instruct",
    "falcon3-7b": "tiiuae/Falcon3-7B-Instruct",
}
MAX_TOKENS = {"mmlu": 8, "triviaqa": 32, "ethics_cs": 8, "ethics_justice": 8, "gsm8k": 768, "math500": 1536}


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("model")
    ap.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=None)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

    items = [json.loads(l) for l in open(ROOT / "datasets/items.jsonl")]
    if args.limit:
        by = {}
        for it in items:
            by.setdefault(it["dataset"], []).append(it)
        items = [it for v in by.values() for it in v[: args.limit]]

    name = MODELS[args.model]
    max_len = 4096
    llm = LLM(model=name, dtype="bfloat16", max_model_len=max_len, gpu_memory_utilization=0.85,
              seed=42, trust_remote_code=True)
    tok = llm.get_tokenizer()

    def render(prompt):
        msgs = [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}]
        kw = {"enable_thinking": False} if "Qwen3" in name else {}
        return tok.apply_chat_template(msgs, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True, **kw)

    prompts = [render(it["prompt"]) for it in items]
    params = [SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=MAX_TOKENS[it["dataset"]], logprobs=1, seed=42)
              for it in items]
    t0 = time.time()
    outs = llm.generate(prompts, params)
    dt = time.time() - t0

    out_dir = ROOT / "results/model_outputs"
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    suffix = f".limit{args.limit}" if args.limit else ""
    with open(out_dir / f"{args.model}{suffix}.jsonl", "w") as f:
        for it, o in zip(items, outs):
            c = o.outputs[0]
            p0 = None
            if c.logprobs:
                lp = c.logprobs[0][c.token_ids[0]].logprob
                p0 = math.exp(lp)
            f.write(json.dumps({"id": it["id"], "text": c.text, "first_tok_prob": p0,
                                "n_tokens": len(c.token_ids), "finish": c.finish_reason}) + "\n")
    meta = {"model": name, "n_items": len(items), "seconds": dt, "max_model_len": max_len,
            "temperature": 0.0, "max_tokens": MAX_TOKENS}
    json.dump(meta, open(out_dir / f"{args.model}{suffix}.meta.json", "w"), indent=2)
    print(f"done {args.model}: {len(items)} items in {dt:.0f}s")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Run one model (vLLM, greedy) over all items and save raw outputs.

Usage: python src/generate.py <model_key> [--limit N]
Output: results/model_outputs/<model_key>.jsonl with {id, text, first_tok_prob, n_tokens}.
`first_tok_prob` is the probability of the first generated token, a single-model confidence baseline
(meaningful for the direct-answer tasks; for CoT tasks it is not used).
"""
import argparse
import json
import math
import time
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent

MODELS = {
    "qwen2.5-7b": "Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct",
    "qwen3-8b": "Qwen/Qwen3-8B",
    "llama3.1-8b": "meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct",
    "phi3-mini": "microsoft/Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct",
    "gemma-7b": "google/gemma-7b-it",
    "olmo3-7b": "allenai/Olmo-3-7B-Instruct",
    "granite3.3-8b": "ibm-granite/granite-3.3-8b-instruct",
    "falcon3-7b": "tiiuae/Falcon3-7B-Instruct",
}
MAX_TOKENS = {"mmlu": 8, "triviaqa": 32, "ethics_cs": 8, "ethics_justice": 8, "gsm8k": 768, "math500": 1536}


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("model")
    ap.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=None)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

    items = [json.loads(l) for l in open(ROOT / "datasets/items.jsonl")]
    if args.limit:
        by = {}
        for it in items:
            by.setdefault(it["dataset"], []).append(it)
        items = [it for v in by.values() for it in v[: args.limit]]

    name = MODELS[args.model]
    max_len = 4096
    llm = LLM(model=name, dtype="bfloat16", max_model_len=max_len, gpu_memory_utilization=0.85,
              seed=42, trust_remote_code=True)
    tok = llm.get_tokenizer()

    def render(prompt):
        msgs = [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}]
        kw = {"enable_thinking": False} if "Qwen3" in name else {}
        return tok.apply_chat_template(msgs, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True, **kw)

    prompts = [render(it["prompt"]) for it in items]
    params = [SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=MAX_TOKENS[it["dataset"]], logprobs=1, seed=42)
              for it in items]
    t0 = time.time()
    outs = llm.generate(prompts, params)
    dt = time.time() - t0

    out_dir = ROOT / "results/model_outputs"
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    suffix = f".limit{args.limit}" if args.limit else ""
    with open(out_dir / f"{args.model}{suffix}.jsonl", "w") as f:
        for it, o in zip(items, outs):
            c = o.outputs[0]
            p0 = None
            if c.logprobs:
                lp = c.logprobs[0][c.token_ids[0]].logprob
                p0 = math.exp(lp)
            f.write(json.dumps({"id": it["id"], "text": c.text, "first_tok_prob": p0,
                                "n_tokens": len(c.token_ids), "finish": c.finish_reason}) + "\n")
    meta = {"model": name, "n_items": len(items), "seconds": dt, "max_model_len": max_len,
            "temperature": 0.0, "max_tokens": MAX_TOKENS}
    json.dump(meta, open(out_dir / f"{args.model}{suffix}.meta.json", "w"), indent=2)
    print(f"done {args.model}: {len(items)} items in {dt:.0f}s")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Run one model (vLLM, greedy) over all items and save raw outputs.

Usage: python src/generate.py <model_key> [--limit N]
Output: results/model_outputs/<model_key>.jsonl with {id, text, first_tok_prob, n_tokens}.
`first_tok_prob` is the probability of the first generated token, a single-model confidence baseline
(meaningful for the direct-answer tasks; for CoT tasks it is not used).
"""
import os
os.environ.setdefault("HF_HUB_OFFLINE", "1")  # gated models (Llama, Gemma) are served from the local cache
import argparse
import json
import math
import time
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent

MODELS = {
    "qwen2.5-7b": "Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct",
    "qwen3-8b": "Qwen/Qwen3-8B",
    "llama3.1-8b": "meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct",
    "phi3-mini": "microsoft/Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct",
    "gemma-7b": "google/gemma-7b-it",
    "olmo3-7b": "allenai/Olmo-3-7B-Instruct",
    "granite3.3-8b": "ibm-granite/granite-3.3-8b-instruct",
    "falcon3-7b": "tiiuae/Falcon3-7B-Instruct",
}
MAX_TOKENS = {"mmlu": 8, "triviaqa": 32, "ethics_cs": 8, "ethics_justice": 8, "gsm8k": 768, "math500": 1536}


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("model")
    ap.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=None)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

    items = [json.loads(l) for l in open(ROOT / "datasets/items.jsonl")]
    if args.limit:
        by = {}
        for it in items:
            by.setdefault(it["dataset"], []).append(it)
        items = [it for v in by.values() for it in v[: args.limit]]

    name = MODELS[args.model]
    max_len = 4096
    llm = LLM(model=name, dtype="bfloat16", max_model_len=max_len, gpu_memory_utilization=0.85,
              seed=42, trust_remote_code=True)
    tok = llm.get_tokenizer()

    def render(prompt):
        msgs = [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}]
        kw = {"enable_thinking": False} if "Qwen3" in name else {}
        return tok.apply_chat_template(msgs, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True, **kw)

    prompts = [render(it["prompt"]) for it in items]
    params = [SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=MAX_TOKENS[it["dataset"]], logprobs=1, seed=42)
              for it in items]
    t0 = time.time()
    outs = llm.generate(prompts, params)
    dt = time.time() - t0

    out_dir = ROOT / "results/model_outputs"
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    suffix = f".limit{args.limit}" if args.limit else ""
    with open(out_dir / f"{args.model}{suffix}.jsonl", "w") as f:
        for it, o in zip(items, outs):
            c = o.outputs[0]
            p0 = None
            if c.logprobs:
                lp = c.logprobs[0][c.token_ids[0]].logprob
                p0 = math.exp(lp)
            f.write(json.dumps({"id": it["id"], "text": c.text, "first_tok_prob": p0,
                                "n_tokens": len(c.token_ids), "finish": c.finish_reason}) + "\n")
    meta = {"model": name, "n_items": len(items), "seconds": dt, "max_model_len": max_len,
            "temperature": 0.0, "max_tokens": MAX_TOKENS}
    json.dump(meta, open(out_dir / f"{args.model}{suffix}.meta.json", "w"), indent=2)
    print(f"done {args.model}: {len(items)} items in {dt:.0f}s")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import argparse
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))
from generate import MODELS  # noqa: E402

MIN_FREE_GB = 13.0
MAX_PAR = 3
MAX_TRIES = 40


def free_gb():
    out = subprocess.run(["nvidia-smi", "--query-gpu=index,memory.free", "--format=csv,noheader,nounits"],
                         capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    return {int(a): int(b) / 1024 for a, b in (l.split(",") for l in out.strip().splitlines())}


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=None)
    ap.add_argument("models", nargs="*")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    todo = args.models or list(MODELS)
    suffix = f".limit{args.limit}" if args.limit else ""
    todo = [m for m in todo if not (ROOT / f"results/model_outputs/{m}{suffix}.jsonl").exists()]
    tries = {m: 0 for m in todo}
    running = {}  # model -> (proc, gpu, start)
    while todo or running:
        for m, (p, g, t0) in list(running.items()):
            if p.poll() is not None:
                del running[m]
                ok = (ROOT / f"results/model_outputs/{m}{suffix}.jsonl").exists()
                print(f"[{time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')}] {m} on GPU{g} exited rc={p.returncode} ok={ok} "
                      f"after {time.time() - t0:.0f}s", flush=True)
                if not ok:
                    tries[m] += 1
                    if tries[m] < MAX_TRIES:
                        todo.append(m)
        if todo and len(running) < MAX_PAR:
            busy = {g for _, g, _ in running.values()}
            cand = [(f, g) for g, f in free_gb().items() if g not in busy and f >= MIN_FREE_GB]
            if cand:
                f, g = max(cand)
                m = todo.pop(0)

                time.sleep(60)  # let it claim memory before considering the next launch
                continue

"""Agreement-vs-correctness analysis over all model outputs.

Reads datasets/items.jsonl and results/model_outputs/<model>.jsonl, writes
  results/answers.csv           (long table: item x model -> answer, correct, confidence)
  results/summary.json          (all metrics with bootstrap CIs)
  results/tables/*.csv / *.md   (report tables)
  figures/*.png
Usage: python src/analyze.py [--suffix .limit5]
"""
import argparse
import itertools
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))
from generate import MODELS  # noqa: E402
from parse import correct, equiv, extract  # noqa: E402

DATASETS = ["triviaqa", "mmlu", "gsm8k", "math500", "ethics_cs", "ethics_justice"]
DOMAIN = {"triviaqa": "factual", "mmlu": "factual", "gsm8k": "math", "math500": "math",
          "ethics_cs": "ethics", "ethics_justice": "ethics"}
DIRECT = {"triviaqa", "mmlu", "ethics_cs", "ethics_justice"}  # single-pass answers -> token prob is a confidence
B = 1000
SEED = 42


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ voting

def plurality(dataset, answers, order=None):
    """Plurality answer among `answers` (list, None = unparseable).

    Each distinct answer's support = number of models whose answer is equivalent to it. Ties are broken
    by the fixed model order (deterministic). Returns (answer, support_count, index_of_representative).
    """
    best, best_n, best_i = None, 0, None
    for i, a in enumerate(answers):
        if a is None:
            continue
        n = sum(equiv(dataset, a, b) for b in answers)
        if n > best_n:
            best, best_n, best_i = a, n, i
    return best, best_n, best_i


def loo_agreement(dataset, answers):
    """For each model i: fraction of the *other* models whose answer is equivalent to model i's answer."""
    n = len(answers)
    out = []
    for i, a in enumerate(answers):
        if a is None:
            out.append(0.0)
        else:
            out.append(sum(equiv(dataset, a, answers[j]) for j in range(n) if j != i) / (n - 1))
    return out


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ stats helpers

def safe_auc(y, s):
    y = np.asarray(y)
    if y.min() == y.max():
        return np.nan
    return roc_auc_score(y, s)


def pb_r(y, s):
    y, s = np.asarray(y, float), np.asarray(s, float)
    if y.std() == 0 or s.std() == 0:
        return np.nan
    return float(np.corrcoef(y, s)[0, 1])


def boot_ci(fn, n, rng, b=B):
    """Percentile bootstrap over items; fn(idx) -> statistic."""
    vals = []
    for _ in range(b):
        idx = rng.integers(0, n, n)
        v = fn(idx)
        if v is not None and not np.isnan(v):
            vals.append(v)
    return float(np.percentile(vals, 2.5)), float(np.percentile(vals, 97.5))


def mcnemar_exact(a, b):
    """a, b boolean arrays (correctness of two systems on same items)."""
    n01 = int(np.sum(~a & b))
    n10 = int(np.sum(a & ~b))
    if n01 + n10 == 0:
        return 1.0
    return float(stats.binomtest(n10, n01 + n10, 0.5).pvalue)


def holm(pvals):
    order = np.argsort(pvals)
    m = len(pvals)
    adj = np.empty(m)
    run = 0
    for k, i in enumerate(order):
        run = max(run, (m - k) * pvals[i])
        adj[i] = min(1.0, run)
    return adj


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ main

def load(suffix, models):
    items = [json.loads(l) for l in open(ROOT / "datasets/items.jsonl")]
    items = {it["id"]: it for it in items}
    rows = []
    for m in models:
        for l in open(ROOT / f"results/model_outputs/{m}{suffix}.jsonl"):
            d = json.loads(l)
            it = items[d["id"]]
            a = extract(it["dataset"], d["text"])
            rows.append(dict(id=d["id"], dataset=it["dataset"], model=m, answer=a,
                             correct=correct(it["dataset"], a, it["gold"]),
                             tok_prob=d["first_tok_prob"], seq_prob=float(np.exp(d.get("cum_logprob") or 0)),
                             finish=d["finish"], n_tokens=d["n_tokens"]))
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    return items, df


def per_item(df, models, ds):
    """Wide per-item table for one dataset with agreement statistics."""
    sub = df[df.dataset == ds]
    A = sub.pivot(index="id", columns="model", values="answer")[models]
    C = sub.pivot(index="id", columns="model", values="correct")[models].astype(bool)
    P = sub.pivot(index="id", columns="model", values="seq_prob")[models]
    return A, C, P


def vote_stats(ds, A_rows, C, items, model_idx):
    """Majority/plurality vote over a subset of models; returns (vote_correct, agreement_rate)."""
    vc, ag = [], []
    for iid, answers in A_rows:
        ans = [answers[k] for k in model_idx]
        a, n, _ = plurality(ds, ans)
        vc.append(correct(ds, a, items[iid]["gold"]))
        ag.append(n / len(ans))
    return np.array(vc), np.array(ag)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--suffix", default="")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)
    models = [m for m in MODELS if (ROOT / f"results/model_outputs/{m}{args.suffix}.jsonl").exists()]
    print("models:", models)
    items, df = load(args.suffix, models)
    (ROOT / "results/tables").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (ROOT / "figures").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    df.to_csv(ROOT / f"results/answers{args.suffix}.csv", index=False)

    summary = {"models": models, "datasets": {}}
    item_tables = {}
    for ds in DATASETS:
        A, C, P = per_item(df, models, ds)
        ids = list(A.index)
        n = len(ids)
        A_rows = [(iid, [A.loc[iid, m] if isinstance(A.loc[iid, m], str) else None for m in models]) for iid in ids]
        Cm = C.values  # n x M bool
        acc = Cm.mean(0)
        best = int(np.argmax(acc))

        # --- full-ensemble plurality vote
        vote_c, agree = vote_stats(ds, A_rows, C, items, list(range(len(models))))
        # unanimity / supermajority diagnostics
        n_distinct = []
        for _, ans in A_rows:
            reps = []
            for a in ans:
                if a is not None and not any(equiv(ds, a, r) for r in reps):
                    reps.append(a)
            n_distinct.append(len(reps))
        # mean accuracy across models per item ("item easiness") — oracle quantity, for reference only
        easiness = Cm.mean(1)

        # --- H1/H3: agreement vs plurality-answer correctness
        r = pb_r(vote_c, agree)
        auc = safe_auc(vote_c, agree)
        r_ci = boot_ci(lambda idx: pb_r(vote_c[idx], agree[idx]), n, rng)
        auc_ci = boot_ci(lambda idx: safe_auc(vote_c[idx], agree[idx]), n, rng)

        # --- per-model leave-one-out agreement as confidence for that model's own answer
        loo = np.array([loo_agreement(ds, ans) for _, ans in A_rows])  # n x M
        per_model = {}
        for k, m in enumerate(models):
            y = Cm[:, k]
            d = {"acc": float(acc[k]), "loo_r": pb_r(y, loo[:, k]), "loo_auc": safe_auc(y, loo[:, k]),
                 "parse_fail": float(np.mean([ans[k] is None for _, ans in A_rows]))}
            if ds in DIRECT:
                pk = P[m].values.astype(float)
                d["selfprob_auc"] = safe_auc(y, pk)
                d["selfprob_r"] = pb_r(y, pk)
            per_model[m] = d

        # --- H2: vote vs best model (oracle-chosen best) & vs mean model
        diff = vote_c.mean() - acc[best]
        diff_ci = boot_ci(lambda idx: vote_c[idx].mean() - Cm[idx][:, best].mean(), n, rng)
        p_mc = mcnemar_exact(vote_c, Cm[:, best])
        # all 5-model subsets: vote vs best-in-subset
        sub5 = []
        for S in itertools.combinations(range(len(models)), 5):
            vc5, _ = vote_stats(ds, A_rows, C, items, list(S))
            sub5.append(vc5.mean() - acc[list(S)].max())
        sub5 = np.array(sub5)

        # --- error correlation between model pairs
        E = (~Cm).astype(float)
        phis, kappas, agree_pairs = [], [], []
        for i, j in itertools.combinations(range(len(models)), 2):
            if E[:, i].std() > 0 and E[:, j].std() > 0:
                phis.append(np.corrcoef(E[:, i], E[:, j])[0, 1])
            both_wrong = np.mean(E[:, i] * E[:, j])
            # P(same wrong answer | both wrong)
            same = [equiv(ds, A_rows[t][1][i], A_rows[t][1][j]) for t in range(n) if E[t, i] and E[t, j]]
            agree_pairs.append(np.mean(same) if same else np.nan)
        # "confident consensus but wrong": >= 75% agree and plurality wrong
        hi = agree >= 0.75
        summary["datasets"][ds] = {
            "domain": DOMAIN[ds], "n": n,
            "model_acc": {m: float(acc[k]) for k, m in enumerate(models)},
            "best_model": models[best], "best_acc": float(acc[best]), "mean_model_acc": float(acc.mean()),
            "vote_acc": float(vote_c.mean()), "vote_minus_best": float(diff), "vote_minus_best_ci": diff_ci,
            "vote_minus_mean": float(vote_c.mean() - acc.mean()),
            "mcnemar_p": p_mc,
            "sub5_vote_minus_best_mean": float(sub5.mean()), "sub5_frac_positive": float(np.mean(sub5 > 0)),
            "sub5_min": float(sub5.min()), "sub5_max": float(sub5.max()),
            "agree_r": r, "agree_r_ci": r_ci, "agree_auc": auc, "agree_auc_ci": auc_ci,
            "mean_agreement": float(agree.mean()), "frac_unanimous": float(np.mean(agree == 1)),
            "acc_when_unanimous": float(vote_c[agree == 1].mean()) if np.any(agree == 1) else None,
            "frac_hi_agree": float(hi.mean()),
            "acc_when_hi_agree": float(vote_c[hi].mean()) if hi.any() else None,
            "frac_hi_agree_wrong": float(np.mean(hi & ~vote_c)),
            "mean_error_phi": float(np.nanmean(phis)),
            "mean_same_wrong_answer": float(np.nanmean(agree_pairs)),
            "mean_n_distinct": float(np.mean(n_distinct)),
            "per_model": per_model,
            "loo_auc_mean": float(np.nanmean([v["loo_auc"] for v in per_model.values()])),
            "loo_r_mean": float(np.nanmean([v["loo_r"] for v in per_model.values()])),
        }
        if ds in DIRECT:
            summary["datasets"][ds]["selfprob_auc_mean"] = float(np.nanmean([v["selfprob_auc"] for v in per_model.values()]))
        item_tables[ds] = pd.DataFrame({"id": ids, "agreement": agree, "vote_correct": vote_c,
                                        "easiness": easiness, "n_distinct": n_distinct})
        item_tables[ds].to_csv(ROOT / f"results/tables/items_{ds}{args.suffix}.csv", index=False)
        s = summary["datasets"][ds]
        print(f"{ds:15s} best={s['best_acc']:.3f} vote={s['vote_acc']:.3f} diff={diff:+.3f} r={r:.3f} "
              f"AUC={auc:.3f} looAUC={s['loo_auc_mean']:.3f} phi={s['mean_error_phi']:.3f}")

    # Holm across datasets for McNemar
    ps = np.array([summary["datasets"][d]["mcnemar_p"] for d in DATASETS])
    for d, pa in zip(DATASETS, holm(ps)):
        summary["datasets"][d]["mcnemar_p_holm"] = float(pa)

    # domain-level pooled r / AUC (pool items of the two datasets in each domain)
    summary["domains"] = {}
    for dom in ["factual", "math", "ethics"]:
        t = pd.concat([item_tables[d] for d in DATASETS if DOMAIN[d] == dom])
        y, s_ = t.vote_correct.values, t.agreement.values
        summary["domains"][dom] = {"r": pb_r(y, s_), "auc": safe_auc(y, s_),
                                   "r_ci": boot_ci(lambda idx: pb_r(y[idx], s_[idx]), len(y), rng),
                                   "auc_ci": boot_ci(lambda idx: safe_auc(y[idx], s_[idx]), len(y), rng)}
    # bootstrap difference in r between domains
    for a, b in [("factual", "ethics"), ("math", "ethics")]:
        ta = pd.concat([item_tables[d] for d in DATASETS if DOMAIN[d] == a])
        tb = pd.concat([item_tables[d] for d in DATASETS if DOMAIN[d] == b])
        diffs = []
        for _ in range(B):
            ia = rng.integers(0, len(ta), len(ta)); ib = rng.integers(0, len(tb), len(tb))
            diffs.append(pb_r(ta.vote_correct.values[ia], ta.agreement.values[ia])
                         - pb_r(tb.vote_correct.values[ib], tb.agreement.values[ib]))
        diffs = np.array(diffs)
        summary["domains"][f"r_diff_{a}_minus_{b}"] = {"ci": [float(np.percentile(diffs, 2.5)), float(np.percentile(diffs, 97.5))],
                                                     "p_one_sided": float(np.mean(diffs <= 0))}

    json.dump(summary, open(ROOT / f"results/summary{args.suffix}.json", "w"), indent=2, default=float)
    make_tables(summary, args.suffix)
    if not args.suffix:
        make_figures(summary, item_tables, df, models)


def make_tables(S, suffix):
    rows = []
    for d in DATASETS:
        s = S["datasets"][d]
        rows.append({"dataset": d, "domain": s["domain"], "best model": f"{s['best_model']} ({s['best_acc']:.3f})",
                     "mean model acc": round(s["mean_model_acc"], 3), "vote acc": round(s["vote_acc"], 3),
                     "vote − best (95% CI)": f"{s['vote_minus_best']*100:+.1f} [{s['vote_minus_best_ci'][0]*100:+.1f}, {s['vote_minus_best_ci'][1]*100:+.1f}]",
                     "McNemar p (Holm)": f"{s['mcnemar_p_holm']:.3g}",
                     "5-subset vote − best (mean)": f"{s['sub5_vote_minus_best_mean']*100:+.1f}",
                     "r (95% CI)": f"{s['agree_r']:.3f} [{s['agree_r_ci'][0]:.2f}, {s['agree_r_ci'][1]:.2f}]",
                     "AUROC (95% CI)": f"{s['agree_auc']:.3f} [{s['agree_auc_ci'][0]:.2f}, {s['agree_auc_ci'][1]:.2f}]",
                     "LOO AUROC (mean)": round(s["loo_auc_mean"], 3),
                     "self-prob AUROC (mean)": round(s.get("selfprob_auc_mean", np.nan), 3),
                     "error φ": round(s["mean_error_phi"], 3),
                     "P(same wrong | both wrong)": round(s["mean_same_wrong_answer"], 3),
                     "unanimous %": round(100 * s["frac_unanimous"], 1),
                     "acc | unanimous": None if s["acc_when_unanimous"] is None else round(s["acc_when_unanimous"], 3),
                     "≥75% agree but wrong %": round(100 * s["frac_hi_agree_wrong"], 1)})
    t = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    t.to_csv(ROOT / f"results/tables/main{suffix}.csv", index=False)
    open(ROOT / f"results/tables/main{suffix}.md", "w").write(t.to_markdown(index=False))
    acc = pd.DataFrame({d: S["datasets"][d]["model_acc"] for d in DATASETS})
    acc.loc["plurality vote"] = [S["datasets"][d]["vote_acc"] for d in DATASETS]
    open(ROOT / f"results/tables/accuracy{suffix}.md", "w").write(acc.round(3).to_markdown())
    print(acc.round(3))


def make_figures(S, item_tables, df, models):
    import matplotlib
    matplotlib.use("Agg")
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
    colors = {"factual": "#2a6fdb", "math": "#1a9e77", "ethics": "#d95f02"}

    # Fig 1: accuracy of the plurality answer as a function of agreement level (calibration-style)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(13, 3.8), sharey=True)
    for ax, dom in zip(axes, ["factual", "math", "ethics"]):
        for d, ls in zip([x for x in DATASETS if DOMAIN[x] == dom], ["-", "--"]):
            t = item_tables[d]
            g = t.groupby(t.agreement.round(3)).agg(acc=("vote_correct", "mean"), n=("vote_correct", "size"))
            g = g[g.n >= 5]
            ax.plot(g.index, g.acc, ls, marker="o", color=colors[dom], label=d)
        ax.plot([0, 1], [0, 1], ":", color="grey", lw=1)
        ax.set_title(dom); ax.set_xlabel("agreement rate (fraction of 8 models on plurality answer)")
        ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8); ax.set_xlim(0.1, 1.02); ax.set_ylim(0, 1.02)
    axes[0].set_ylabel("accuracy of plurality answer")
    fig.suptitle("Plurality-answer accuracy vs inter-model agreement (bins with ≥5 items)")
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(ROOT / "figures/agreement_vs_accuracy.png", dpi=150); plt.close(fig)

    # Fig 2: r and AUROC with CIs per dataset
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 3.8))
    xs = np.arange(len(DATASETS))
    for ax, key, lab, band in [(axes[0], "agree_r", "point-biserial r", (0.4, 0.6)),
                               (axes[1], "agree_auc", "AUROC", (0.7, 0.8))]:
        v = [S["datasets"][d][key] for d in DATASETS]
        lo = [S["datasets"][d][key + "_ci"][0] for d in DATASETS]
        hi = [S["datasets"][d][key + "_ci"][1] for d in DATASETS]
        c = [colors[DOMAIN[d]] for d in DATASETS]
        ax.bar(xs, v, color=c, alpha=0.85)
        ax.errorbar(xs, v, yerr=[np.array(v) - lo, np.array(hi) - v], fmt="none", ecolor="k", capsize=3)
        ax.axhspan(*band, color="grey", alpha=0.15, label="hypothesised range (factual/math)")
        if key == "agree_r":
            ax.axhline(0.2, color="#d95f02", ls="--", lw=1, label="hypothesised ethics ceiling (0.2)")
        else:
            ax.axhline(0.5, color="grey", ls=":", lw=1)
        ax.set_xticks(xs); ax.set_xticklabels(DATASETS, rotation=20); ax.set_ylabel(lab)
        ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8)
    fig.suptitle("Agreement rate as an unsupervised correctness signal (95% bootstrap CI)")
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(ROOT / "figures/r_auc_by_dataset.png", dpi=150); plt.close(fig)

    # Fig 3: model accuracies vs vote
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 3.8))
    w = 0.8 / (len(models) + 1)
    cmap = plt.get_cmap("tab10")
    for k, m in enumerate(models):
        ax.bar(xs + k * w, [S["datasets"][d]["model_acc"][m] for d in DATASETS], w, color=cmap(k), label=m)
    ax.bar(xs + len(models) * w, [S["datasets"][d]["vote_acc"] for d in DATASETS], w, color="k", label="plurality vote")
    ax.set_xticks(xs + 0.4); ax.set_xticklabels(DATASETS); ax.set_ylabel("accuracy")
    ax.legend(ncol=5, fontsize=7, frameon=False, loc="upper center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.12))
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(ROOT / "figures/accuracy_models_vs_vote.png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight"); plt.close(fig)

    # Fig 4: pairwise error correlation heatmaps (factual vs ethics vs math)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(DATASETS), figsize=(3.2 * len(DATASETS), 3.2))
    for ax, d in zip(axes, DATASETS):
        sub = df[df.dataset == d].pivot(index="id", columns="model", values="correct")[models].astype(float)
        E = 1 - sub.values
        M = np.corrcoef(E.T)
        ax.imshow(M, vmin=-0.2, vmax=1, cmap="viridis")
        ax.set_title(f"{d}\nmean φ={S['datasets'][d]['mean_error_phi']:.2f}", fontsize=9)
        ax.set_xticks(range(len(models))); ax.set_yticks(range(len(models)))
        ax.set_xticklabels(models, rotation=90, fontsize=6); ax.set_yticklabels(models if ax is axes[0] else [], fontsize=6)
    fig.suptitle("Pairwise correlation of error indicators", y=1.02)
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(ROOT / "figures/error_correlation.png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight"); plt.close(fig)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

toolu_01QbHu7ZQ5wbVBeR75GS26NB.content:
"""Agreement-vs-correctness analysis over all model outputs.

Reads datasets/items.jsonl and results/model_outputs/<model>.jsonl, writes
  results/answers.csv           (long table: item x model -> answer, correct, confidence)
  results/summary.json          (all metrics with bootstrap CIs)
  results/tables/*.csv / *.md   (report tables)
  figures/*.png
Usage: python src/analyze.py [--suffix .limit5]
"""
import argparse
import itertools
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))
from generate import MODELS  # noqa: E402
from parse import correct, equiv, extract  # noqa: E402

DATASETS = ["triviaqa", "mmlu", "gsm8k", "math500", "ethics_cs", "ethics_justice"]
DOMAIN = {"triviaqa": "factual", "mmlu": "factual", "gsm8k": "math", "math500": "math",
          "ethics_cs": "ethics", "ethics_justice": "ethics"}
DIRECT = {"triviaqa", "mmlu", "ethics_cs", "ethics_justice"}  # single-pass answers -> token prob is a confidence
B = 1000
SEED = 42


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ voting

def plurality(dataset, answers, order=None):
    """Plurality answer among `answers` (list, None = unparseable).

    Each distinct answer's support = number of models whose answer is equivalent to it. Ties are broken
    by the fixed model order (deterministic). Returns (answer, support_count, index_of_representative).
    """
    best, best_n, best_i = None, 0, None
    for i, a in enumerate(answers):
        if a is None:
            continue
        n = sum(equiv(dataset, a, b) for b in answers)
        if n > best_n:
            best, best_n, best_i = a, n, i
    return best, best_n, best_i


def loo_agreement(dataset, answers):
    """For each model i: fraction of the *other* models whose answer is equivalent to model i's answer."""
    n = len(answers)
    out = []
    for i, a in enumerate(answers):
        if a is None:
            out.append(0.0)
        else:
            out.append(sum(equiv(dataset, a, answers[j]) for j in range(n) if j != i) / (n - 1))
    return out


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ stats helpers

def safe_auc(y, s):
    y = np.asarray(y)
    if y.min() == y.max():
        return np.nan
    return roc_auc_score(y, s)


def pb_r(y, s):
    y, s = np.asarray(y, float), np.asarray(s, float)
    if y.std() == 0 or s.std() == 0:
        return np.nan
    return float(np.corrcoef(y, s)[0, 1])


def boot_ci(fn, n, rng, b=B):
    """Percentile bootstrap over items; fn(idx) -> statistic."""
    vals = []
    for _ in range(b):
        idx = rng.integers(0, n, n)
        v = fn(idx)
        if v is not None and not np.isnan(v):
            vals.append(v)
    return float(np.percentile(vals, 2.5)), float(np.percentile(vals, 97.5))


def mcnemar_exact(a, b):
    """a, b boolean arrays (correctness of two systems on same items)."""
    n01 = int(np.sum(~a & b))
    n10 = int(np.sum(a & ~b))
    if n01 + n10 == 0:
        return 1.0
    return float(stats.binomtest(n10, n01 + n10, 0.5).pvalue)


def holm(pvals):
    order = np.argsort(pvals)
    m = len(pvals)
    adj = np.empty(m)
    run = 0
    for k, i in enumerate(order):
        run = max(run, (m - k) * pvals[i])
        adj[i] = min(1.0, run)
    return adj


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ main

def load(suffix, models):
    items = [json.loads(l) for l in open(ROOT / "datasets/items.jsonl")]
    items = {it["id"]: it for it in items}
    rows = []
    for m in models:
        for l in open(ROOT / f"results/model_outputs/{m}{suffix}.jsonl"):
            d = json.loads(l)
            it = items[d["id"]]
            a = extract(it["dataset"], d["text"])
            rows.append(dict(id=d["id"], dataset=it["dataset"], model=m, answer=a,
                             correct=correct(it["dataset"], a, it["gold"]),
                             tok_prob=d["first_tok_prob"], seq_prob=float(np.exp(d.get("cum_logprob") or 0)),
                             finish=d["finish"], n_tokens=d["n_tokens"]))
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    return items, df


def per_item(df, models, ds):
    """Wide per-item table for one dataset with agreement statistics."""
    sub = df[df.dataset == ds]
    A = sub.pivot(index="id", columns="model", values="answer")[models]
    C = sub.pivot(index="id", columns="model", values="correct")[models].astype(bool)
    P = sub.pivot(index="id", columns="model", values="seq_prob")[models]
    return A, C, P


def vote_stats(ds, A_rows, C, items, model_idx):
    """Majority/plurality vote over a subset of models; returns (vote_correct, agreement_rate)."""
    vc, ag = [], []
    for iid, answers in A_rows:
        ans = [answers[k] for k in model_idx]
        a, n, _ = plurality(ds, ans)
        vc.append(correct(ds, a, items[iid]["gold"]))
        ag.append(n / len(ans))
    return np.array(vc), np.array(ag)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--suffix", default="")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)
    models = [m for m in MODELS if (ROOT / f"results/model_outputs/{m}{args.suffix}.jsonl").exists()]
    print("models:", models)
    items, df = load(args.suffix, models)
    (ROOT / "results/tables").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (ROOT / "figures").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    df.to_csv(ROOT / f"results/answers{args.suffix}.csv", index=False)

    summary = {"models": models, "datasets": {}}
    item_tables = {}
    for ds in DATASETS:
        A, C, P = per_item(df, models, ds)
        ids = list(A.index)
        n = len(ids)
        A_rows = [(iid, [A.loc[iid, m] if isinstance(A.loc[iid, m], str) else None for m in models]) for iid in ids]
        Cm = C.values  # n x M bool
        acc = Cm.mean(0)
        best = int(np.argmax(acc))

        # --- full-ensemble plurality vote
        vote_c, agree = vote_stats(ds, A_rows, C, items, list(range(len(models))))
        # unanimity / supermajority diagnostics
        n_distinct = []
        for _, ans in A_rows:
            reps = []
            for a in ans:
                if a is not None and not any(equiv(ds, a, r) for r in reps):
                    reps.append(a)
            n_distinct.append(len(reps))
        # mean accuracy across models per item ("item easiness") — oracle quantity, for reference only
        easiness = Cm.mean(1)

        # --- H1/H3: agreement vs plurality-answer correctness
        r = pb_r(vote_c, agree)
        auc = safe_auc(vote_c, agree)
        r_ci = boot_ci(lambda idx: pb_r(vote_c[idx], agree[idx]), n, rng)
        auc_ci = boot_ci(lambda idx: safe_auc(vote_c[idx], agree[idx]), n, rng)

        # --- per-model leave-one-out agreement as confidence for that model's own answer
        loo = np.array([loo_agreement(ds, ans) for _, ans in A_rows])  # n x M
        per_model = {}
        for k, m in enumerate(models):
            y = Cm[:, k]
            d = {"acc": float(acc[k]), "loo_r": pb_r(y, loo[:, k]), "loo_auc": safe_auc(y, loo[:, k]),
                 "parse_fail": float(np.mean([ans[k] is None for _, ans in A_rows]))}
            if ds in DIRECT:
                pk = P[m].values.astype(float)
                d["selfprob_auc"] = safe_auc(y, pk)
                d["selfprob_r"] = pb_r(y, pk)
            per_model[m] = d

        # --- H2: vote vs best model (oracle-chosen best) & vs mean model
        diff = vote_c.mean() - acc[best]
        diff_ci = boot_ci(lambda idx: vote_c[idx].mean() - Cm[idx][:, best].mean(), n, rng)
        p_mc = mcnemar_exact(vote_c, Cm[:, best])
        # all 5-model subsets: vote vs best-in-subset
        sub5 = []
        for S in itertools.combinations(range(len(models)), 5):
            vc5, _ = vote_stats(ds, A_rows, C, items, list(S))
            sub5.append(vc5.mean() - acc[list(S)].max())
        sub5 = np.array(sub5)

        # --- error correlation between model pairs
        E = (~Cm).astype(float)
        phis, kappas, agree_pairs = [], [], []
        for i, j in itertools.combinations(range(len(models)), 2):
            if E[:, i].std() > 0 and E[:, j].std() > 0:
                phis.append(np.corrcoef(E[:, i], E[:, j])[0, 1])
            both_wrong = np.mean(E[:, i] * E[:, j])
            # P(same wrong answer | both wrong)
            same = [equiv(ds, A_rows[t][1][i], A_rows[t][1][j]) for t in range(n) if E[t, i] and E[t, j]]
            agree_pairs.append(np.mean(same) if same else np.nan)
        # "confident consensus but wrong": >= 75% agree and plurality wrong
        hi = agree >= 0.75
        summary["datasets"][ds] = {
            "domain": DOMAIN[ds], "n": n,
            "model_acc": {m: float(acc[k]) for k, m in enumerate(models)},
            "best_model": models[best], "best_acc": float(acc[best]), "mean_model_acc": float(acc.mean()),
            "vote_acc": float(vote_c.mean()), "vote_minus_best": float(diff), "vote_minus_best_ci": diff_ci,
            "vote_minus_mean": float(vote_c.mean() - acc.mean()),
            "mcnemar_p": p_mc,
            "sub5_vote_minus_best_mean": float(sub5.mean()), "sub5_frac_positive": float(np.mean(sub5 > 0)),
            "sub5_min": float(sub5.min()), "sub5_max": float(sub5.max()),
            "agree_r": r, "agree_r_ci": r_ci, "agree_auc": auc, "agree_auc_ci": auc_ci,
            "mean_agreement": float(agree.mean()), "frac_unanimous": float(np.mean(agree == 1)),
            "acc_when_unanimous": float(vote_c[agree == 1].mean()) if np.any(agree == 1) else None,
            "frac_hi_agree": float(hi.mean()),
            "acc_when_hi_agree": float(vote_c[hi].mean()) if hi.any() else None,
            "frac_hi_agree_wrong": float(np.mean(hi & ~vote_c)),
            "mean_error_phi": float(np.nanmean(phis)),
            "mean_same_wrong_answer": float(np.nanmean(agree_pairs)),
            "mean_n_distinct": float(np.mean(n_distinct)),
            "per_model": per_model,
            "loo_auc_mean": float(np.nanmean([v["loo_auc"] for v in per_model.values()])),
            "loo_r_mean": float(np.nanmean([v["loo_r"] for v in per_model.values()])),
        }
        if ds in DIRECT:
            summary["datasets"][ds]["selfprob_auc_mean"] = float(np.nanmean([v["selfprob_auc"] for v in per_model.values()]))
        item_tables[ds] = pd.DataFrame({"id": ids, "agreement": agree, "vote_correct": vote_c,
                                        "easiness": easiness, "n_distinct": n_distinct})
        item_tables[ds].to_csv(ROOT / f"results/tables/items_{ds}{args.suffix}.csv", index=False)
        s = summary["datasets"][ds]
        print(f"{ds:15s} best={s['best_acc']:.3f} vote={s['vote_acc']:.3f} diff={diff:+.3f} r={r:.3f} "
              f"AUC={auc:.3f} looAUC={s['loo_auc_mean']:.3f} phi={s['mean_error_phi']:.3f}")

    # Holm across datasets for McNemar
    ps = np.array([summary["datasets"][d]["mcnemar_p"] for d in DATASETS])
    for d, pa in zip(DATASETS, holm(ps)):
        summary["datasets"][d]["mcnemar_p_holm"] = float(pa)

    # domain-level pooled r / AUC (pool items of the two datasets in each domain)
    summary["domains"] = {}
    for dom in ["factual", "math", "ethics"]:
        t = pd.concat([item_tables[d] for d in DATASETS if DOMAIN[d] == dom])
        y, s_ = t.vote_correct.values, t.agreement.values
        summary["domains"][dom] = {"r": pb_r(y, s_), "auc": safe_auc(y, s_),
                                   "r_ci": boot_ci(lambda idx: pb_r(y[idx], s_[idx]), len(y), rng),
                                   "auc_ci": boot_ci(lambda idx: safe_auc(y[idx], s_[idx]), len(y), rng)}
    # bootstrap difference in r between domains
    for a, b in [("factual", "ethics"), ("math", "ethics")]:
        ta = pd.concat([item_tables[d] for d in DATASETS if DOMAIN[d] == a])
        tb = pd.concat([item_tables[d] for d in DATASETS if DOMAIN[d] == b])
        diffs = []
        for _ in range(B):
            ia = rng.integers(0, len(ta), len(ta)); ib = rng.integers(0, len(tb), len(tb))
            diffs.append(pb_r(ta.vote_correct.values[ia], ta.agreement.values[ia])
                         - pb_r(tb.vote_correct.values[ib], tb.agreement.values[ib]))
        diffs = np.array(diffs)
        summary["domains"][f"r_diff_{a}_minus_{b}"] = {"ci": [float(np.percentile(diffs, 2.5)), float(np.percentile(diffs, 97.5))],
                                                     "p_one_sided": float(np.mean(diffs <= 0))}

    json.dump(summary, open(ROOT / f"results/summary{args.suffix}.json", "w"), indent=2, default=float)
    make_tables(summary, args.suffix)
    if not args.suffix:
        make_figures(summary, item_tables, df, models)


def make_tables(S, suffix):
    rows = []
    for d in DATASETS:
        s = S["datasets"][d]
        rows.append({"dataset": d, "domain": s["domain"], "best model": f"{s['best_model']} ({s['best_acc']:.3f})",
                     "mean model acc": round(s["mean_model_acc"], 3), "vote acc": round(s["vote_acc"], 3),
                     "vote − best (95% CI)": f"{s['vote_minus_best']*100:+.1f} [{s['vote_minus_best_ci'][0]*100:+.1f}, {s['vote_minus_best_ci'][1]*100:+.1f}]",
                     "McNemar p (Holm)": f"{s['mcnemar_p_holm']:.3g}",
                     "5-subset vote − best (mean)": f"{s['sub5_vote_minus_best_mean']*100:+.1f}",
                     "r (95% CI)": f"{s['agree_r']:.3f} [{s['agree_r_ci'][0]:.2f}, {s['agree_r_ci'][1]:.2f}]",
                     "AUROC (95% CI)": f"{s['agree_auc']:.3f} [{s['agree_auc_ci'][0]:.2f}, {s['agree_auc_ci'][1]:.2f}]",
                     "LOO AUROC (mean)": round(s["loo_auc_mean"], 3),
                     "self-prob AUROC (mean)": round(s.get("selfprob_auc_mean", np.nan), 3),
                     "error φ": round(s["mean_error_phi"], 3),
                     "P(same wrong | both wrong)": round(s["mean_same_wrong_answer"], 3),
                     "unanimous %": round(100 * s["frac_unanimous"], 1),
                     "acc | unanimous": None if s["acc_when_unanimous"] is None else round(s["acc_when_unanimous"], 3),
                     "≥75% agree but wrong %": round(100 * s["frac_hi_agree_wrong"], 1)})
    t = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    t.to_csv(ROOT / f"results/tables/main{suffix}.csv", index=False)
    open(ROOT / f"results/tables/main{suffix}.md", "w").write(t.to_markdown(index=False))
    acc = pd.DataFrame({d: S["datasets"][d]["model_acc"] for d in DATASETS})
    acc.loc["plurality vote"] = [S["datasets"][d]["vote_acc"] for d in DATASETS]
    open(ROOT / f"results/tables/accuracy{suffix}.md", "w").write(acc.round(3).to_markdown())
    print(acc.round(3))


def make_figures(S, item_tables, df, models):
    import matplotlib
    matplotlib.use("Agg")
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
    colors = {"factual": "#2a6fdb", "math": "#1a9e77", "ethics": "#d95f02"}

    # Fig 1: accuracy of the plurality answer as a function of agreement level (calibration-style)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(13, 3.8), sharey=True)
    for ax, dom in zip(axes, ["factual", "math", "ethics"]):
        for d, ls in zip([x for x in DATASETS if DOMAIN[x] == dom], ["-", "--"]):
            t = item_tables[d]
            g = t.groupby(t.agreement.round(3)).agg(acc=("vote_correct", "mean"), n=("vote_correct", "size"))
            g = g[g.n >= 5]
            ax.plot(g.index, g.acc, ls, marker="o", color=colors[dom], label=d)
        ax.plot([0, 1], [0, 1], ":", color="grey", lw=1)
        ax.set_title(dom); ax.set_xlabel("agreement rate (fraction of 8 models on plurality answer)")
        ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8); ax.set_xlim(0.1, 1.02); ax.set_ylim(0, 1.02)
    axes[0].set_ylabel("accuracy of plurality answer")
    fig.suptitle("Plurality-answer accuracy vs inter-model agreement (bins with ≥5 items)")
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(ROOT / "figures/agreement_vs_accuracy.png", dpi=150); plt.close(fig)

    # Fig 2: r and AUROC with CIs per dataset
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 3.8))
    xs = np.arange(len(DATASETS))
    for ax, key, lab, band in [(axes[0], "agree_r", "point-biserial r", (0.4, 0.6)),
                               (axes[1], "agree_auc", "AUROC", (0.7, 0.8))]:
        v = [S["datasets"][d][key] for d in DATASETS]
        lo = [S["datasets"][d][key + "_ci"][0] for d in DATASETS]
        hi = [S["datasets"][d][key + "_ci"][1] for d in DATASETS]
        c = [colors[DOMAIN[d]] for d in DATASETS]
        ax.bar(xs, v, color=c, alpha=0.85)
        ax.errorbar(xs, v, yerr=[np.array(v) - lo, np.array(hi) - v], fmt="none", ecolor="k", capsize=3)
        ax.axhspan(*band, color="grey", alpha=0.15, label="hypothesised range (factual/math)")
        if key == "agree_r":
            ax.axhline(0.2, color="#d95f02", ls="--", lw=1, label="hypothesised ethics ceiling (0.2)")
        else:
            ax.axhline(0.5, color="grey", ls=":", lw=1)
        ax.set_xticks(xs); ax.set_xticklabels(DATASETS, rotation=20); ax.set_ylabel(lab)
        ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8)
    fig.suptitle("Agreement rate as an unsupervised correctness signal (95% bootstrap CI)")
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(ROOT / "figures/r_auc_by_dataset.png", dpi=150); plt.close(fig)

    # Fig 3: model accuracies vs vote
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 3.8))
    w = 0.8 / (len(models) + 1)
    cmap = plt.get_cmap("tab10")
    for k, m in enumerate(models):
        ax.bar(xs + k * w, [S["datasets"][d]["model_acc"][m] for d in DATASETS], w, color=cmap(k), label=m)
    ax.bar(xs + len(models) * w, [S["datasets"][d]["vote_acc"] for d in DATASETS], w, color="k", label="plurality vote")
    ax.set_xticks(xs + 0.4); ax.set_xticklabels(DATASETS); ax.set_ylabel("accuracy")
    ax.legend(ncol=5, fontsize=7, frameon=False, loc="upper center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.12))
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(ROOT / "figures/accuracy_models_vs_vote.png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight"); plt.close(fig)

    # Fig 4: pairwise error correlation heatmaps (factual vs ethics vs math)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(DATASETS), figsize=(3.2 * len(DATASETS), 3.2))
    for ax, d in zip(axes, DATASETS):
        sub = df[df.dataset == d].pivot(index="id", columns="model", values="correct")[models].astype(float)
        E = 1 - sub.values
        M = np.corrcoef(E.T)
        ax.imshow(M, vmin=-0.2, vmax=1, cmap="viridis")
        ax.set_title(f"{d}\nmean φ={S['datasets'][d]['mean_error_phi']:.2f}", fontsize=9)
        ax.set_xticks(range(len(models))); ax.set_yticks(range(len(models)))
        ax.set_xticklabels(models, rotation=90, fontsize=6); ax.set_yticklabels(models if ax is axes[0] else [], fontsize=6)
    fig.suptitle("Pairwise correlation of error indicators", y=1.02)
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(ROOT / "figures/error_correlation.png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight"); plt.close(fig)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
